summary: S-1 and S-2 are resolved, and the whole of section 4.5 (Prop 4.5, Lem 4.8(r1), Ex 4.5a Q*, Prop 4.6, Lem 4.7) is valid. The countermodels are now independent, with exactly one hypothesis violated per countermodel. PA-1 and PA-2 are resolved, coverage is complete, and the R5 spec is precise. One blocking regression remains: the generic (O', H') proofs of Prop 4.1(i'), Prop 4.1(iii) and Lem 5.2 assume that the starting history satisfies F1 or F2, although Def 1.8 lets a frame be any subset of S and A5, A7 and A9 are closure properties only. The statements are true, and the base case is unaffected. Minimal fix: define frames as subsets of the base frame H.

proof_check.note: h1 = h[sigma, f=inf] and h2 = h[sigma*, f=inf] satisfy F1 vacuously; h3 satisfies it by assumption. All three are in H' by A5 applied to h. The chain uses A2, A1, A2.
h[p, inf] satisfies F1 vacuously, so no F1 premise is needed in h.
'Each step satisfies F1' presupposes F1 in h, which is not a hypothesis. Repair: first pass to h[sigma, f=inf] (A5, A2).

Step 1 uses 'By F1 in h'. Counter-scenario: H' = H u {h0}, where h0 has an issue act b with f(b)=1, v(b)=p, sigma(1)=q. This pair satisfies A1, A2, A4, A5 and A7, but h0[sigma', f'] fails F1, so it is not in H'. Repair: also set f' = inf on every F1-violating act. All other steps check.
H is a subset of F1 and F2.
SC1 and SC2 suffice; no F1 or F2 premise is needed.

regressions.issue: The generic proofs use F1 or F2 in the starting history. Frames are arbitrary subsets of S (Def 1.8), and A5, A7 and A9 are closure properties only. The statements are true; the proofs are invalid as written.
mu_h(lambda) = w1 is stated unconditionally; it should hold only when w1 is in W_h.
Def 4.9 is called a criterion for S2 and S3; independence bears on S3 (veridicality), not on S2.
